Hi Jordan and Priya,

Thanks again for taking time today — appreciated the candid conversation about the payments pipeline and latency-sensitive fraud checks. Quick recap and a couple of suggested next steps so we can align on fit: 

- Recap of call:
  • Primary goal: reduce p99 inference latency on authorization checks from ~180ms to sub-80ms while keeping cost per decision flat.
  • Key constraints: existing HSM latency for key lookups; PostgreSQL-based enrichment calls; strict retention rules for transaction traces.
  • Successful outcome: integrated runtime with prefix caching for known user flows + fallback routing to a cheaper model for low-risk transactions.

- What we demonstrated:
  • How Redwood’s serving runtime keeps KV cache locality across bursts
  • Example rollout plan (canary by region + automated fallback)
  • Ballpark economics for a 200k monthly decisions workload (attached deck)

- Ask: does the technical approach match what you were expecting? Any red flags we missed?

Proposed next steps (pick one):
1) 15-minute pricing/ops sync to nail down unit economics and SLA needs
2) 30-minute technical deep-dive with your infra lead to map integration points

I attached the demo deck and my annotated discovery notes. If you prefer, I can also put together a short mutual action plan that maps owners and timelines.

Thanks — looking for a quick thumbs up on whether this looks like a fit so we can prioritize.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
